question: Assume today is 2026-08-16. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan in August 2026, as it will be first reported in the Japan National Tourism Organization's (JNTO) monthly estimate.

target.what: Number of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan (inbound international visitors) as estimated by the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) in its monthly press release. The JNTO estimate counts foreign nationals entering Japan for any purpose (tourism, business, visiting friends/relatives, etc.) ba
target.cadence: Monthly, typically released around the 15th-20th of the following month (e.g., August data released mid-September 2026).
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the information cutoff (2026-08-16). The estimate is a preliminary figure subject to revision. The definition counts arrivals, not unique visitors; a person entering multiple times is counted multiple times. The JNTO estimate is based on immigration records an

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 foreign visitor arrivals can be projected from the same month in previous years, adjusted for recent year-on-year growth trends. August is a peak month due to summer holidays. The relationship is: target = August 2025 value × (1 + recent YoY growth rate).
candidates.data_to_find: JNTO monthly estimates for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, and the most recent months available before the cutoff (e.g., June 2026, July 2026 if published). Also monthly YoY growth rates for 2026 year-to-date. Minimum evidence: August 2025 value and the latest 2026 monthly YoY growth rate.
search_hints: JNTO monthly foreign visitor arrivals August 2025

candidates.hypothesis: JNTO estimates are derived from MOJ immigration records. The number of foreign nationals entering Japan in August 2026 can be approximated by MOJ monthly entry data, which may be published with a similar lag. The relationship is: JNTO estimate ≈ MOJ foreign entries minus certain categories (e.g., re-entries of foreign residents).
candidates.data_to_find: MOJ monthly statistics on foreign nationals entering Japan for recent months (e.g., June 2026, July 2026) and historical August data. Also the ratio of JNTO estimate to MOJ foreign entries to calibrate the coverage adjustment. Minimum evidence: MOJ foreign entries for a recent month and the corresponding JNTO estimate.
search_hints: 出入国在留管理庁 外国人入国者数 月別 2026
MOJ immigration statistics foreign entries Japan monthly

candidates.hypothesis: Foreign visitor arrivals are a subset of total international passenger arrivals at Japanese airports and seaports. If total international arrivals and the foreign visitor share are known, the target can be estimated. The relationship is: target = total international arrivals × foreign visitor share. August is peak season, so capacity and load factors are high.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly international passenger arrivals at major Japanese airports (Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, Fukuoka, etc.) for August 2025 and recent 2026 months. Also the share of foreign visitors among international arrivals (from JNTO or airport surveys). Minimum evidence: total international arrivals for a recent month and the foreign visitor share.
search_hints: Japan international passenger arrivals August 2025 airport statistics

candidates.hypothesis: Foreign visitor arrivals are constrained by available international flight seats and accommodation capacity. If seat capacity and load factors are known, arrivals can be estimated. The relationship is: target ≈ international seat capacity × load factor × foreign visitor share. August is peak, so load factors are high.
candidates.data_to_find: International flight seat capacity to Japan for August 2026 (from OAG, airline schedules, or airport authorities). Load factors for international flights to Japan. Hotel occupancy rates and foreign guest ratios in major cities for August 2026. Minimum evidence: seat capacity and load factor for a recent month.

candidates.data_to_find: Exchange rate (JPY/USD, JPY/CNY, JPY/KRW) trends in 2026. Any new visa policies for key source markets (China, South Korea, Taiwan, US, etc.) effective in 2026. Travel advisories from major source countries. Minimum evidence: exchange rate level and any major policy changes.

candidates.data_to_find: Japan Tourism Agency (JTA) or JNTO forecasts for 2026 inbound visitors. Seasonal share of August in annual arrivals (historical average). Minimum evidence: annual forecast for 2026 and August share.

candidates.perspective: Seasonal patterns and source market mix
candidates.hypothesis: August has a consistent seasonal pattern in Japan's inbound tourism, with a peak due to summer holidays from East Asia. The share of August in annual arrivals is stable. The relationship is: target = annual arrivals × August share. Also, source market mix (South Korea, China, Taiwan, etc.) affects total.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly seasonal factors for August from 2015-2025 (August arrivals / annual arrivals). Source market breakdown for August in recent years. Minimum evidence: August share for 2024 and 2025.
search_hints: Japan inbound tourism seasonal August share

methods.rationale: Projects August 2026 from the observed August 2025 JNTO estimate (p18) using a YoY change factor (a1) that reflects the 2026 China slump and non-China strength. Uses the first-half 2026 cumulative (p3) to annualize 2026 arrivals, then applies the August seasonal share (a2) to estimate August 2026. This route assumes H2 2026 runs at the same average monthly pace as H1 2026, which may be conservative if the China drag eases or optimistic if it worsens. methods.rationale: Own-history route: August 2025 JNTO estimate (p18) scaled by an assumed YoY change factor (a1) reflecting the recent negative trend (p2, p54) and the strong 2025 base. Decomposition route: August 2025 total (p18) scaled by an ex-China YoY factor (a4), then adjusted for the change in China share from the 2026 Jan-May level (p36) to the assumed August 2026 share (a5). This explicitly models the China collapse (p30, p36) and ex-China strength (p32). The formula assumes the ex-China base and China share are the dominant drivers; it is a rough bridge and shares the p18 base with m1.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
